sections.history: Haridwaramangalam, whose Tevaram name is Tiruaradaiperumpazhi, lies about 10 km west of Alangudi in the Valangaiman taluk of Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, and is also counted among the Pancha Aranya Kshetrams, the five forest shrines of the Kumbakonam country, as the Vanni vanam. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Paathaleswarar — 'lord of Patala, the netherworld' — in the sanctum, with the goddess Alankaravalli in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the vanni (shami) tree, which gives the place its forest name. The temple is revered as a rina-vimochana sthalam, a place where worship is held to free devotees from debts.
sections.legends: The playful sthala legend tells that just before his wedding with Parvati, Shiva went into hiding underground, in Patala, in sport. The gods searched for the vanished bridegroom, and Vishnu — Hari — opened a door, a dwara, into the underworld to find him. From this deed the town takes its name, Haridwaramangalam, 'the auspicious place of Hari's door,' and the lord is called Paathaleswarar, lord of the netherworld. As a Pancha Aranya shrine of the vanni forest and a rina-vimochana sthalam, it is sought for relief from debts and burdens.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Devotees seeking release from debts, and pilgrims making the round of the Pancha Aranya forests, include Haridwaramangalam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Haridwaramangalam the pilgrim comes to a shrine of hidden grace, where Shiva once vanished into the earth in play and Vishnu opened a door to find him. Before Paathaleswarar and Alankaravalli, beneath the vanni of the forest shrine, the visitor feels the lightness of a divine game and the hope of release from every burden.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Haridwaramangalam is about 10 km west of Alangudi, in the Valangaiman taluk of Tiruvarur district (PIN 612802). Kumbakonam and Valangaiman are the nearest rail heads, with buses via Alangudi and local taxis to the village.
